title: ecdh_wrap_cek: duplicated AES-KW arm code across kek_len 16 and 32
description: encrypt.rs ecdh_wrap_cek() lines 434-461: the 16-byte and 32-byte kek_len arms are structurally identical — both do try_into().map_err(...)?, then KwAes{128,256}::new(...).wrap_key(...).map_err(...). The only difference is the array size and the Kw type. Suggested rewrite: use a helper macro or a two-branch function that takes the KW operation as a closure. Alternatively, encode the KW type selection in a trait object dispatch. As-is, a future change to error handling must be made in two places — the second arm is invisible when reading the first.
close_reason: The two arms use KwAes128 and KwAes256 — distinct concrete types in Rust's type system. Factoring out the duplication would require trait objects or macros, adding complexity with no benefit for 2 arms. Won't-fix.
